svg.title: Detection lab virtual network topology
svg.text: Detection lab · virtual network on pve01
How the 802.1Q trunk, the VLAN-aware bridge and OPNsense connect every zone
one cable to Fa0/3 · 100 Mb/s full
Each port adds or strips its own VLAN tag. Only OPNsense can move traffic between VLANs.
default deny · NAT from lab to WAN
What crosses the switch, and what stays inside the host
VM to VM across zones never leaves pve01: VM → vmbr0 (tag) → vtnet1 → pf →
vtnet1 → vmbr0 (new tag) → VM. The switch never sees it.
Only three kinds of traffic use the Fa0/3 trunk: VLAN 100 (OPNsense WAN and
Proxmox management), VLAN 50 (physical Kali) and VLAN 10 (switch 10.10.10.2).
Untagged frames on Fa0/3 land in native VLAN 999, which goes nowhere.
VMs never see tags. The bridge port adds the tag on the way in and strips it
on the way out. OPNsense is the one VM that receives tagged frames (vtnet1).
Proxmox management (vmbr0.100) bypasses OPNsense on purpose (DD-010).
